record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.context_brief: Need for realizing polyhedral metrics as polyhedra
record.original_question: When a suitable polyhedral metric is available for the variational grid problem, is it mathematically or computationally necessary to realize that metric by an actual polyhedron, or is it enough to run numerical simulation and minimization directly on manifolds with polyhedral metrics?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. In variational grid generation one seeks a mapping (a grid) from a parameter domain into a target region by minimizing a functional whose integrand depends on the Jacobian of the mapping and on a prescribed Riemannian or polyhedral "control" metric g that encodes the desired local size, shape, and orientation of grid cells. Suppose that the control metric g produced (or required) by such a variational principle is a polyhedral metric on a manifold M, i.e. a metric obtained by gluing finitely many Euclidean simplices along isometries of their faces, so that (M, g) is a flat manifold with conical singularities concentrated on a codimension-2 set.

By a classical theorem of Alexandrov, every polyhedral metric of nonnegative curvature on the 2-sphere can be realized as the induced intrinsic metric on the boundary of a convex polytope in Euclidean 3-space; analogous realization questions exist in higher dimensions and for metrics of mixed curvature signs.

Problem. Decide whether, for the purposes of carrying out numerical simulation and minimization of variational grid-generation functionals with a polyhedral control metric g, it is mathematically or computationally necessary to first construct an isometric realization of (M, g) as an actual polyhedron (e.g. embedded or immersed in some Euclidean space) before performing the optimization, or whether one can equivalently and rigorously formulate and solve the variational problem intrinsically on the abstract manifold-with-polyhedral-metric (M, g) without ever producing such a realization. Provide either:
(a) a proof that an intrinsic formulation on (M, g) is sufficient — including a precise definition of the discrete variational functional on (M, g), an existence/convergence theory for its minimizers, and algorithms that operate solely on the combinatorial-metric data of (M, g); or
(b) a proof that some essential analytic or computational obstruction forces one to realize (M, g) as a polyhedron, identifying the obstruction explicitly.
artifact.category_tag: Variational grid generation with polyhedral metrics
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search reveals continuing work on variational grid generation with control metrics and on variational realization of polyhedral metrics (e.g., Bobenko–Izmestiev for Alexandrov's theorem, and discrete uniformization for ideal hyperbolic polyhedra), but no source was found that conclusively settles whether realizing the polyhedral control metric as an actual polyhedron is necessary, or whether intrinsic minimization on the manifold-with-polyhedral-metric suffices for variational grid generation. The question therefore appears to remain unresolved in the published literature.

status_evidence.title: Ideal Hyperbolic Polyhedra and Discrete Uniformization
status_evidence.snippet: A variational proof of Rivin's realization theorem... equivalent to a discrete uniformization theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Variational realization theorems for polyhedral metrics continue to be developed, but do not directly address the grid-generation need.

status_evidence.title: Variational method for hexahedral grid generation with control metric
status_evidence.snippet: variational method of generating spatial structured grids... functional whose integrand is a dimensionless ratio of metric invariants
status_evidence.claim: Variational grid generation with control metrics is an active research area where the polyhedral-realization question naturally arises.

status_evidence.title: Elements of Alexandrov geometry
status_evidence.snippet: singular surface geometry... topological surfaces with intrinsic metrics... polyhedral surfaces
status_evidence.claim: Intrinsic treatment of polyhedral metrics on manifolds is well developed, suggesting an intrinsic formulation could in principle be possible.
